class: A label laid out as a non-wrapping flex row around a select whose width comes from its longest option pushes the page wider than a phone screen once an option is long; the page then scrolls sideways or cuts the option text off.
mechanism: At 390 px: the Compare's 'Approach to prepare' and 'Approaches in the compare' labels (flex items-center, no wrap, select without max width) made the page 531 px; the editor's Playbook select (min-w-64, no max) made it 399 px.

first_seen.where: GC-MU A5 390 px check in the owner's Chrome
first_seen.evidence: in-frame: compare docScrollW 531 / scrollX 159, editor 399 / 27; hiding adjust-prepare dropped the page to 372

fix: 44cbcb25: labels `flex-wrap min-w-0 max-w-full`, selects `max-w-full`; after: all four page states 372 = 372.

detection.note: Needs a real-browser 390 px check (e2e); jsdom cannot measure it.
